## jig v0.2.0-alpha.7

Servers render with the Unicode 18 text-block build, the switch the alpha.6 notes announced
(#401). Text renders as before unless it contains one of 68 code points newly assigned in
Unicode 18. The legacy relay is being retired: a channel reaches another server only by a
share. All four of alpha.6's known limitations are fixed: the stalled shared channel, the
shared slug, messages from before you joined, and adding someone from another server to an
encrypted channel.

This is an alpha. Pre-1.0 releases make no wire, receipt or storage compatibility guarantee, and
jig has not had an external security audit yet (D27).

### Breaking: servers render with the Unicode 18 text-block build

- **Servers render with the new text-block build** (#401, step 2 of #402). Its component hash
  is now `blake3:99593614ee82449902364ae342cc9d4d671e39c9da0c2d236394908e3c351fb8` (was
  `blake3:8ab0a9eb…5b179`). An operator policy that allows text-block by component hash needs
  the new value; the alpha.6 notes asked operators to add it ahead of this release.
- **Text normalization moves to Unicode 18.** 68 code points newly assigned in Unicode 18 now
  normalize under NFKC. No existing mapping changes and none is removed, so all other text
  renders, and hashes, exactly as before.
- **Verification across the switch:**
  - Clients on alpha.6 or later verify servers on either build.
  - Clients on alpha.5 or older show every render from a server on this release as
    **unverified**, not only messages with the new code points. Never as divergent: a client
    picks the build by the receipt's component hash before it compares an outcome. Upgrading
    the client restores verification.
  - Clients on this release keep the alpha.6 build, pinned by its hash, so they still verify
    servers that have not upgraded.

### Breaking: the legacy relay is retired

The legacy relay is removed over four PRs in this release. Channels reach other servers only
by a share.
- #426 moves the tests that must outlive the relay onto plain shares.
- #439 stops sending relayed posts.
- #453 stops taking them, and removes the relay's catch-up.
- #470 deletes the `naively_accept_peer_relayed_creates` flag.

- **A server neither sends nor takes relayed posts** (#439, #453). A peer on an earlier release
  no longer sees this server's posts in its own channel of the same name, and its posts no
  longer land here. Those copies caused the #357 stall. **Share any channel that reached peers
  only through the relay.**
  - A peer on an earlier release still subscribes to the relay's stream. Every such
    subscription, from a listed peer or not, is answered as malformed (`BAD_JSON`). The peer's
    catch-up request is logged at DEBUG.
  - The connection stays up, so the peer's shares keep working. A peer that is not listed is
    still refused when a share is offered (`NOT_A_PEER`), and its operator sees the
    `BAD_JSON` error in its log.
- **Delete `federation.naively_accept_peer_relayed_creates` from your config before
  upgrading** (#470). The test-only setting is removed. A config that still sets it, `true` or
  `false`, does not boot, and the error names the key. `install.sh` restarts the server, so
  delete the line first.
- **`jig_federation_relayed_refused_total` is no longer exported** (#453), and the
  `relayed-into-sequenced-channel` WARN is gone. Nothing is relayed to refuse. Remove both from
  dashboards and alerts.
- **The relay's catch-up tables are dropped** (#453): `catch_up_cursors` and `catch_up_seen`
  held peer URLs and block CIDs, nothing a user wrote. A downgraded server creates them again,
  empty, and resumes from its newest held block.

### Fixes

- **A shared channel that stalled before alpha.6 heals after upgrading, with nothing to do**
  (#441, fixes #427).
  - This is the stall `jig-server contracts list` shows. Your own channel of the same name is
    unchanged.
  - The follower now keeps a block it already holds in its own channel in both chains, each
    under its own record. The follower asks its owners for what it is missing every few
    seconds, so the channel catches up within that and the stall stops being listed.
  - If you ended the share to get around the stall, the owner shares it again
    (`jig channel share`) for it to catch up.
  - Downgrading shows a hole in that channel at each formerly stalled position, and a client
    holding caught-up history (#414) warns that it is not whole there. Nothing is lost:
    upgrading again reads it back.
- **A shared channel and one of the follower's own can share a slug** (#430, fixes #388).
  - A client pins channels by id, so it no longer refuses the second one as
    `ChannelReplaced`.
  - The slug still names the server's own channel, so reach the shared one by its id. `jig`
    prints a note on stderr naming both ids, and `channel list` marks both lines.
  - A pin file from alpha.6 or earlier is rekeyed by id when first opened.
- **A server's own encrypted channels keep their MLS state by channel id, not slug** (#444,
  fixes #432). A server that gives a slug to a new channel, such as a re-created `#team`, no
  longer hands the new channel the old one's group.
  - State an older build filed under a slug is filed under the id its pin names when `jig`
    first opens it. The slug entry stays, so an older build still finds its groups.
  - A slug with no pin is left where it is, with a warning.
- **A `jig channel create` retry no longer adopts another device's channel** (#458, fixes
  #455). When a create got no answer and the slug turns out to be listed, `jig` now checks the
  listed channel's creation block against the group it left pending.
  - It adopts the group only if the two match.
  - Otherwise, for example when another device under the same identity created the slug, it
    discards the pending group and says the channel exists and how to join it. Before, this
    device would send in a group the channel's members were not in.
- **A peer listed in another letter case is found by its DID** (#470, fixes #460). Before, a
  peer whose `expected_did` was typed in another case connected, but its shares were refused
  `NOT_A_PEER` and its stream quota fell back to the default. A published peer's DID is already
  canonical and was not affected.
  - Listing one peer twice in different letter case with different quotas is now refused at
    boot as a duplicate, as the same spelling twice already was.
- **Encrypted messages sent before you joined show as `🔒 [sent before you joined]`**, not as
  `[cannot decrypt: …]` (#433, fixes #431).
  - The device records the epochs it has been a member for.
  - A message is relabelled only when it is signed and its group and epoch show it came from
    before your join, or from a gap after you were removed. Every other failure keeps its
    reason.
  - Groups joined before this release have no record, so their earlier messages still show
    `cannot decrypt`. Groups joined after upgrading get the label.
- **The server's fixed retry waits are spread out** (#435). The waits for a missed render
  deadline (1 s) and for `OWNER_UNREACHABLE` (5 s) are now drawn uniformly from 0.5–1.5× their
  nominal value. Refused clients no longer all come back at once. Rate-limit waits are
  unchanged, because they give the time until a token is back.
- **You can add someone from another server to an encrypted channel** (#440, fixes #421). Use
  `jig channel add <slug> <did> --via <server-url>`, where `--via` names a server the member
  uses.
  - When the owner's server has no key package for the member, `jig` asks one of the member's
    key-package custodians. A custodian is a server listed in the member's signed reachability
    record.
  - The custodian releases one package and logs it. `jig` checks that the package is the
    member's before it commits, so a custodian can withhold a package but not substitute one.
  - If no custodian releases one, nothing is committed, and the error names each server tried.
- **A follower hands a shared channel's posts to its bridges** (#475, for #454). Each carried
  post goes to the bridges of the managed DIDs among the channel's members, except the sender.
  A member removed from the channel gets their own removal.
  - The follower executes nothing for a carried block, so the block a bridge gets lists no
    receipt.
  - The email bridge, the one bridge shipped, declines carried posts for now, because it
    routes by slug, and does not mark them seen. Email members get them once #474 lands.

### Behaviour changes

- **Withdrawing a custodian stops its releases to other servers only** (#440, JEP-0005 rule
  21a). A member who publishes a reachability record without a server can still be added to
  that server's own channels from its stock. Ending those adds is a separate request (JEP-0017
  R2).
- **`jig server custody off` ends a server's custody of your key packages** (#461, JEP-0017
  R1). `jig server custody on` restores it.
  - `off` publishes a reachability record without the configured server, there and, best
    effort, to each other server the record lists. Nameservers are not told yet.
  - It then rotates this device's keys. It publishes a fresh last-resort package at that
    server, and deletes the keys of the old one and of the packages the release log shows went
    to other servers.
  - Packages already released are not recalled; an add made with one of them after this gives
    the adder a group you are not in.
  - Run it on each device, or let each device rotate its keys on its next contact with that
    server. A device never lists a withdrawn server again on its own.
  - Members of that server can still add you.
- **`jig server local-adds off` stops others adding you to the server's own channels** (#463,
  JEP-0017 R2). `jig server local-adds on` allows it again.
  - Channels you are in stay as they are, and you can still join a channel yourself.
  - Members trying to add you see `LOCAL_ADDS_ENDED`, or `MEMBER_DECLINED` if they fetched a
    package elsewhere. `jig` treats both as final and does not try other custodians.
  - With both custody and local adds ended at a server, that server deletes your stock there
    and refuses new uploads, and `jig` deletes the matching keys and stops publishing packages
    to it.
- **A member by aged proof alone self-joins channels as a `guest`** (#473, JEP-0014 rule 8).
  A DID in the member pool only by an aged admission proof gets capacity, but a
  `join = member` channel now takes recorded members only.
  - It applies to joins checked after upgrading. Memberships made before it are unchanged.

### Protocol

- **JEP-0002 rule 7 describes `retry_after_ms` on an ordinary error frame** (#435).
  - A server SHOULD spread a wait it picks itself over 0.5–1.5×.
  - A client that retries SHOULD wait `retry_after_ms` plus a random extra of up to half of
    it, and SHOULD NOT retry sooner.
- **JEP-0005 rule 13:** a block the follower already holds in another channel is kept in both
  chains, each under its own record, never moved or re-signed (#441).
- **Key-package custody** (#440):
  - JEP-0005 gains rule 21a, a signed `jig-kp-request-v1` addressed to one custodian, and
    rule 21b, the interim release policy.
  - JEP-0004 rule 21 names the reachability routes, `PUT` and `GET /api/v1/reach/{did}`.
  - The Encryption chapter describes `POST /api/v1/custody/{did}/requests`. A DID reads its
    own release log at `GET /api/v1/custody/{did}/releases`.
  - A last-resort package now replaces the one a server holds only when the upload is signed
    by its DID over the request body (#461). An older last-resort package that leaked through
    custody can no longer displace a usable one.
  - A stored withdrawal retires the DID's earlier custody releases, so a repeated request is
    not answered with a package whose key its owner deleted (#461).
  - A request proof is verified even with authenticated reads off, and a bad one is refused
    rather than read as anonymous (#461).
- **Ending local adds** (#463, JEP-0017 rules 16 to 19):
  - A member signs a `jig-local-adds-v1` marker and sends it to `PUT /api/v1/local-adds/{did}`.
    The server keeps the marker with the highest `seq`. Test vectors are in `vectors/0017/`.
  - While local adds are ended:
    - `GET /api/v1/mls/key-packages/{did}` answers `403 LOCAL_ADDS_ENDED`;
    - a custody request for a channel this server sequences is refused the same way;
    - a `member-add` of the DID to a channel this server sequences is refused
      `403 MEMBER_DECLINED`, and the block is not stored.
  - With custody ended too, the server deletes the DID's stock and refuses uploads with
    `403 NOT_STOCKED_HERE`.
  - The stock route gains `stocked`, which is `false` in that state. The field is additive, and
    a server without it is read as `true`. A client deletes its keys on `stocked: false` only,
    never on an empty stock.
- **A server can declare its ruleset** (#471, JEP-0002 rules 2 and 12, JEP-0009 rule 4):
  - A hello can ask for the `ruleset` capability. Only then does the signed welcome name the
    ruleset, under tag 5: `{id, version, hash, url}`, or a 0 when the server declares none. A
    client that does not ask gets the same welcome bytes as before.
  - The `server-manifest` block carries the ruleset beside its document, under the metadata
    key `server_ruleset`, with `supersedes` naming the entry it replaces. It is kept out of the
    document, which older clients would refuse. A change of ruleset publishes a new manifest
    entry.
  - A client that asked refuses a welcome that grants a feature it did not ask for. It also
    refuses one whose ruleset differs from the one its cited manifest declares, or that names
    none while the manifest declares one. A withheld ruleset is a refusal, not evidence
    against the server.
  - A client checks a fetched ruleset against the declared hash, `id` and `version`. Its pins
    cache now records the ruleset with the manifest, so the same manifest naming another
    ruleset is checked again.

### Operators

- **Key packages are released within hourly limits** (#440). Both the new custody route and
  the existing `GET /api/v1/mls/key-packages/{did}` follow `[custody] per_member_per_hour`
  (default 10) and `per_requester_per_hour` (default 20). Every release is logged in the
  member's release log, with its kind: `custody` for a release to another server's
  requester, `local` for a take by the key-package route.
  - Adds on one server share the member's budget. Adding one member to more than 10 encrypted
    channels in an hour is refused with `429 RATE_LIMITED` until the hour rolls over. Raise
    `per_member_per_hour` if that is too low.
  - With authenticated reads off (`require_authenticated_reads = false`), all anonymous
    callers share one `per_requester_per_hour` budget: by default 20 key-package takes an hour,
    across all members. Turn authenticated reads on, or raise the limit, if that is too few.
- **PROXY protocol v2 behind a TLS-passthrough proxy** (#423, for #399). List the proxy in
  `[server.proxy_protocol] trusted` (addresses or CIDRs) and have it send v2: HAProxy
  `send-proxy-v2`, or nginx 1.31.4+ `stream` with `proxy_protocol v2` (nginx's
  `proxy_protocol on` sends v1, which is refused). Each client then gets its own per-address
  rate bucket and relay slots, instead of sharing the proxy's.
  - It fails closed: a connection from a listed proxy without a valid v2 header within
    `header_timeout_ms` (default 5000) is closed, never served as the proxy. Headers over
    536 bytes are refused, which a load balancer adding many TLVs can exceed.
  - A connection from any other address is served as before. Forwarded HTTP headers are never
    trusted. A valid `LOCAL` header, such as the proxy's own health check, keeps the proxy's
    address. The nameserver does not read PROXY protocol yet (#419).
- **Members by aged proof draw from a share of the member pool** (#451). `[auth.pools]
  aged_share_pct` (default 25) caps how much of the member share DIDs that are members only by
  an aged admission proof can use, so a batch of proofs that age in together cannot crowd out
  recorded members.
  - It is a cap, not a reservation: recorded members can still use the whole member share.
  - `0` makes an aged proof no membership, so those DIDs stay strangers; `100` lets them use
    the whole member share.
  - A burst so small that the aged allowance would be under one write is raised to one write,
    with a warning at boot. Such a config booted before and still boots.
- **jig-server shuts down gracefully on SIGTERM or SIGINT** (#437).
  - It stops accepting connections, and closes each WebSocket with code 1001 (going away) so
    clients reconnect promptly.
  - It gives requests in flight up to `[server] shutdown_drain_ms` (default 5000, at most
    300000) to finish, then exits 0. A second signal cuts the drain short.
  - A block being ingested when the drain runs out is stored whole or not at all.
  - Once the drain ends, blocking work still running gets up to 1 s more before the process
    exits. `install.sh` waits 10 s for the server it replaces, and systemd's `TimeoutStopSec`
    defaults to 90 s, so keep the drain a few seconds under both.
- **The nameserver shuts down gracefully too** (#472). It stops accepting connections, gives
  requests in flight up to `[network] shutdown_drain_ms` (default 5000, at most 300000) to
  finish, then exits 0. A second signal cuts the drain short, and `0` cuts at once.
  - `JIG_NS_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_MS` overrides it. A value that does not parse, or one over the
    maximum, refuses boot.
  - A registration, rotation or renewal being written when the drain is cut is stored whole or
    not at all. A rotation now expires the old binding and stores the new one in one
    transaction.
  - As with jig-server, keep the drain a few seconds under `TimeoutStopSec`. See the
    nameserver's `OPERATOR_GUIDE.md`.
- **`[ruleset] path` declares a ruleset** (#471). It names a signed ruleset document; `url`
  optionally names an `https://` mirror that clients fetch it from instead.
  - The server serves it at `GET /api/v1/ruleset/<hash>`, names it in the manifest log and in
    welcomes to clients that ask, and logs `declaring a ruleset` at boot.
  - Boot is refused if the file is missing or does not verify. It is also refused if the
    ruleset's pool shares (stranger, invited and aged) differ from what `[auth.pools]` enforces,
    or the pools are off, and the error names both values.
  - The pool shares are all of a ruleset a server enforces today. Its standing and other
    parameters are not applied yet.
- **`[custody] release`** is `"open"` (the default) or `"closed"`. It stands in for every
  DID's release policy until DIDs sign their own.
- **`jig` publishes a reachability record by default.** The record lists the configured server
  for the client's DID, which links the DID to that server for anyone who asks it.
  - To stop this, set `[server] publish_reachability = false` in `cli.toml`. Key packages are
    still stocked.
  - A record that is already published stays until it is replaced.

### Dependencies

- **unicode-normalization 0.1.25 → 0.1.26**, pinned exactly in `text-block`, because its NFKC
  tables are part of the render output (#401). The canonical text-block artifact is rebuilt
  with it, which also brings wit-bindgen 0.57 into the guest bindings.
- **rusqlite 0.41 → 0.43 and libsqlite3-sys 0.39 → 0.40** (#413, #469). 0.43 is a breaking
  release of rusqlite. The bundled SQLite is still 3.54.1. A test now fails if a later bump
  bundles an SQLite older than 3.54.1, the release with the #381 fix (#434).
- **wasmtime 50.0.3** (#447), with cranelift 0.137.3. 50.0.3 is the patched release on the 50
  line for RUSTSEC-2026-0566 through -0573. The minimum wasmtime version in the manifests is
  now 50.0.3, so a fresh resolve cannot pick an affected release.
- **Render receipts name the new engine.** They carry wasmtime 50.0.3 and a new engine config
  fingerprint, which covers the wasmtime version. Fuel costs are unchanged and
  `FUEL_SCHEDULE_VERSION` stays 0.2.0, so a receipt's fuel numbers are the same as before.
- **Minor bumps** (#469): rand 0.10.4, clap 4.6.8, uuid 1.29.3, zeroize 1.9.2 and ipnet
  2.12.2, with syn 3.0.10 in the lockfile.
- **jsonwebtoken is removed** (#465). Nothing used it. Its `pem` and `simple_asn1`
  dependencies leave the lockfile with it.
- **url 2.5.8 → 2.5.9**, with form_urlencoded 1.2.3, for RUSTSEC-2026-0592 (#476).
- **chrono and humantime are now flagged unmaintained** (RUSTSEC-2026-0543 and
  RUSTSEC-2026-0542). Neither reports a vulnerability, and neither has a safe upgrade yet.
  Both are listed as ignored in `deny.toml` until #445 replaces them (#446).

### Docs and spec

- **The block-ABI vectors swap builds** (#401): the canonical `text-block-*` vectors now carry
  the Unicode 18 build, and `text-block-prev-*` carry the alpha.6 build. Neither build's
  outcomes moved.
- **Verifiable standing (R2.1), specified, with two parts implemented.** No server computes or
  checks standing this way yet. A server can declare a ruleset, and enforces only its pool
  shares (#471). The `aged_share` bound on members by aged proof is enforced (#451). Both are
  under Operators.
  - **JEP-0009 rules 35–52** (#418): standing is a deterministic function,
    `R = f(ruleset, epoch log, epoch)`.
    - An epoch closes on cosigned checkpoint time, not on a count of log positions.
    - Signed standing checkpoints carry four kinds of fraud proof: arithmetic, omission,
      fabrication and equivocation.
    - The standing key is salted, so a DID's standing is not published unless it opts in.
    - Membership by an aged admission proof needs the subject's `ack`. It is bounded by
      `aged_share` in JEP-0008 rule 23.
  - **JEP-0009 rules 1 and 5** (#452):
    - A subject's `ack` names the subject: `{v, ruleset_hash, server, subject, at}`.
    - Signed objects carry no `kid`. Each object's rule says whose key verifies it: a ruleset
      document is verified by one of its `authors`, an `ack` by its `subject`, a report by its
      `reporter`.
    - `jig-core` gains a `ruleset` module that parses, re-encodes and signs ruleset documents.
      No server uses it yet, and nothing produces acks.
  - **JEP-0016 rules 1, 6 and 6b** (#448):
    - Epochs are JEP-0009's.
    - Every commit, reveal and beacon-reveal window closes only once both its position
      count and a cosigned-time floor have passed.
    - Proof of work never feeds standing. Its one bridge is aged-proof membership.
  - **Four reference rulesets** (#420): `jig-reference`, `high-sec`, `community` and
    `null-sec`. They are drafted as data, with a reference model and standing traces under
    `vectors/0009/`.
  - **JEP-0008 registers `alg = 2`, Equi-X** (#425), with a verification budget (rule 10a) and
    a three-release migration plan. Nothing implements it yet; every verifier still uses
    `alg = 1`.

- **JEP-0017, leaving a server** (#457), defines three separate requests a member signs, none
  inferred from another:
  - **R1, end custody:** stop releasing the member's key packages to other servers. This is
    JEP-0005 rule 21a's withdrawal. It ships in this release: the server side in #440, and
    `jig server custody off|on` with its key rotation in #461.
  - **R2, end local adds:** stop adding the member to this server's own channels. It ships in
    this release (#463), as `jig server local-adds off|on`.
  - **R3, erase and leave:** remove the member's data from this server, keep a tombstone, and
    stop serving the member. Specified, not implemented.
  - A request binds only the server it names. Key packages already released are not recalled;
    they stay usable until their lifetime ends or the member deletes their keys.

- **JEP-0015, authenticated writes** (#358, Draft): a server must know who submits each local
  block, from a proof bound to the WebSocket handshake or the REST request, and refuse a block
  its submitter did not sign. Relayed and carried blocks, and server-originated ones, are the
  named exemptions. Not implemented yet.
  - Its rule 5 now names PROXY protocol v2 from listed proxies as how clients behind one proxy
    get their own address (#459, #423).
- **JEP-0016 states its fractions in ppm** and its sampling thresholds as exact integer
  arithmetic, so every implementation draws the same set (#422).
- **The threat register's AB-03** states the per-peer limits (#416).
- **The audit scope** says what key-package custody (F2 Task 8) and MLS channels across
  servers (Task 7) still lack, and where JEP-0017 stands (#468).

- **The upgrade-path check now starts from alpha.6 too** (#471), as well as alpha.1 and
  alpha.2. It also checks that alpha.6's `jig` still verifies the welcome and manifest of a
  server on this build that declares a ruleset.

### Known limitations

- **Members on the email bridge don't get a shared channel's posts yet** (#474). The follower
  hands them to the bridge (#475), which declines them until it routes by channel id.
- **Adding someone from another server works through `--via` only for now** (#440). Finding
  their custodian from their verified name needs the nameserver to serve their reachability
  record, and `jig` doesn't send one at registration yet.
- **`jig dm` to someone on another server** still needs their key packages on the DM's server
  (#440).
- **Many identities that each pass a custodian's admission** can still draw a member's
  ordinary key packages down to the last-resort one, within the per-member limit. Signed
  release policies are the planned fix (JEP-0005 rule 21b).
- **A device removed from an encrypted channel while it ran an earlier release**, then added
  again after upgrading, has no record of that earlier membership. Its unread messages from
  then can show as "sent before you joined". They are unreadable either way (#433).

### Threat-register entries mitigated

Statuses are as of this release. *Partial* means part of the entry's decision is implemented;
the register says which part.

| Entry | What this release does | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OP-09 Federation abuse | A server neither sends nor takes a block outside a share, so the legacy relay is gone in both directions (#439, #453) | Partial |
